notes: Two no-op turns in ONE `hermes chat` session separated by an inline `/model <name> --provider lmstudio --session` slash. Hermes writes no transcript file — the daemon observes the shared SQLite store at $HERMES_HOME/state.db (ProcessOwnedStore) — so session_birth is anchored UNPINNED to recording start (the transient proc-<PID> pre-session carries the ready birth; the store-backed row is INSERTed only on the first user message) and every later phase pins to t1_start via same_session_as, the verified opencode/hermes sibling shape. THE STATE PHASES ARE EXPECTED TO PASS: a CLI /model writes NO messages row (the display_kind='model_switch' marker is written by tui_gateway/server.py only, never by `hermes chat`), so sessions.message_count does not grow, Watcher.reconcile emits no EventActivity, and the switch window holds ready with no working/waiting flicker — which model_switch_window asserts with duration_at_least_ms 6000. known_failing is NOT set: it guards state phases only (validate/expected_test.go errors if a passing report carries the flag), and those pass. NO observations block is pinned, for the same reason as the 2-1 sibling: `of verify` hard-asserts only against the newest recording's replay-golden summary (validate/observations.go ValidateObservations → readGoldenSummary; no golden → Skipped, Pass=true), and the hermes driver exports no store→JSONL transcript today (grep finds no json_object export in driver-interactive.sh, unlike opencode's), so a hermes recording yields no transcript.jsonl and hence no golden — a pin here would be a promise nothing checks. THE SCENARIO'S CENTRAL CLAIM IS THEREFORE CARRIED BY THE RECIPE'S verify[], NOT BY A MACHINE ASSERTION, and it is expected to fail on the live surface: irrlicht reads ModelName from `sessions.model`, and hermes never rewrites that column on a mid-session CLI switch (update_session_model has no caller under cli.py/hermes_cli — only tui_gateway and the messaging gateway; update_token_counts rewrites it only while api_call_count==0, 'issue #51607'; create_session's upsert COALESCEs), so ModelName stays model A at t2_end. The per-model truth lives one table over in session_model_usage, keyed by the live model per API call, which the adapter does not read — daemon=bug, an adapter read away from full. record captures both `SELECT model FROM sessions WHERE id=<id>` (one model) and `SELECT model, last_seen FROM session_model_usage WHERE session_id=<id>` (two models) as the issue's primary evidence. Model A is not pinned either: the driver launches a bare `hermes chat` with no --model flag, so A is the recording home's config.yaml model.default (gpt-5.6-luna in the maintainer's home). Per issue #440 the durable claim is that the model CHANGES, not the concrete pair — if the recording home lacks the lmstudio provider, record substitutes any second reachable model.

text: A hermes session appears in ready shortly after `hermes chat` launch (anchored UNPINNED so the proc-<PID> pre-session cannot steal identity); nothing ever enters waiting — neither turn uses a tool
Turn 1's user prompt drives the store-backed session ready → working under model A (the config default; this send is also what materializes the sessions row)
Turn 1 completes back to ready on the same store-backed session (assistant row with finish_reason='stop' → turn_done); SessionMetrics.ModelName = model A

The inline `/model … --provider lmstudio --session` runs locally with no LLM round-trip and writes no messages row, so message_count does not grow and the watcher emits nothing: state stays ready with no working/waiting flicker
Turn 2's user prompt drives the SAME session ready → working, now served by model B

Turn 2 completes back to ready on the same session. Spec: SessionMetrics.ModelName = model B (latest wins) and TotalTokens after t2_end > after t1_end. Tokens do accumulate (sessions.input_tokens+output_tokens sum across both models); the model flip is what the daemon cannot see today — asserted in the recipe's verify[] against the live metrics surface, not here
